observed_facts: Current documented model: account, Workspace, Project, folders/assets, Collections, Shares, version stacks and, for Mounted Storage, individual saves. API paths scope project access by account_id and project_id; filenames are not the only resource identity.

The selected asset drives Viewer and Details panels. The Viewer can remain open while browsing other folders in the same Project. Details can expose comments and fields without opening the full player.

Collections are saved metadata-filtered views of a Project/folder source that update in real time without moving assets. Team/public Collections are visible to project members and share appearance changes; Private Collections are personal. Ordinary Project appearance is personal by default.

Custom metadata field definitions live in an account library and can apply across Projects/Workspaces. Copying, moving or duplicating an asset preserves existing metadata. A field need only be defined once; creation/edit access can be limited to Admins.

Copy To retains the source and optionally copies comments. The copying article says the copied URL references the original underlying file and does not double account storage. It explicitly forbids cross-account copying.

Duplicating a Project produces a copy inside the Workspace, excludes existing users, comments and Shares, and optionally includes assets. This is not documented as live-linking an entire production instance.

Version stacks accept mixed asset types, can be reordered, and open the newest version by default. Mounted Storage saves instead nest in version history attached to the current version, with date/time/author evidence. Saves do not add storage; a new version does consume additional capacity.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Preserve a common production/asset/version/save identity across bin, viewer, graph, review and delivery surfaces; store view state separately from media ownership.
[INFERENCE] Model shared definitions, personal views, live Collections and copied production instances as different objects. Copying storage bytes and copying review evidence are separate operations.
limitations: [uncertain] The copying article introduces cross-Project copying but its final FAQ says copies are only permitted between subfolders within the same Project. Exact destination support needs confirmation rather than choosing either contradictory sentence.
[uncertain] The copying article states a 200-asset bulk-operation limit; Project Layout Overview states 1000 in web and 200 in iOS. No definitive current web limit is asserted.

[uncertain] Exact cross-session restoration of selection, scroll position, playhead and panel layout is not established by these sources. Stable panel context within a Project does not prove persistence across reloads.

observed_facts: Not applicable to Frame.io's documented native review/asset workspace as an execution-DAG comparison. Collections and metadata statuses describe organization, not a typed node graph with dependencies and node-level retry semantics.

Official integrations support public API resources, webhooks for upload/status events, and custom Actions surfaced in the Frame.io UI. Workfront Fusion, Zapier and Make are named low/no-code integrations.

The February 2026 recap documents Zapier v1.3.3 custom API calls powered by the official SDK with over 50 API methods; examples include creating workspace/project/folder structures and changing asset metadata. It also describes improved authentication/error detection.

The December 2025 recap documents Firefly Actions beta for Firefly Services customers, including Reframe, Dub and Remove Background, operating on one or 100 assets and organizing results in a new folder. This is an action/batch-output contract, not evidence of a generic native graph.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Expose review/delivery integrations as typed boundaries in FrameForge's own graph, recording provider resource IDs and returned artifacts. An automation trigger or a successful action request should not be relabeled as approved or published output.
limitations: Native node cancellation, partial retry/reuse and execution-trace guarantees are not established by the consulted documentation; this is not a claim that no integration could implement them.
Zapier/Fusion/Make execution history, quotas and retry semantics belong to their own platform contracts and were not tested here.

observed_facts: Standard search discovers media, folders and Projects within an account and supports core metadata such as Status, Keywords, Uploader, Assignee, File Type, Format and Source Filename. Results show Workspace/Project location and matching metadata; View in Source and Copy URL preserve source navigation.

NLP search can query metadata, transcripts and comments; selecting a transcript/comment match navigates to its location. Semantic search finds visual image/video content and matched video moments; current help limits semantic search to Team/Enterprise.

Explicit current search limits include 50 Standard plus 50 AI results, no custom metadata support, no saved-search/convert-to-Collection feature, no facial recognition, and no semantic search for audio. NLP cannot retain conversational history or understand negation. The help FAQ lists version-stack containment and comment timestamps among unsupported AI search fields.

The July 2026 release added a dedicated full-screen search page with query carry-over from the search bar, project/object filters, previews and multi-file actions. Full-screen search availability on all plans does not mean every AI search capability is available on all plans.

Web import supports drag/drop files or folders and explicit upload commands, retains folder structure, stores originals for download and encodes streaming representations. Documented web limits are 500 assets at once, 250 folders, 10 folder levels and 10 concurrent queued upload jobs; the article says Transfer v1.2.0+ avoids those web limits. Maximum asset size is documented as 5 TB.

The December 2025 official recap says Content Credentials reads and preserves uploaded assets' credentials to expose origin and AI-creation information. The July 2026 recap describes Leica SL3-P C2C ingest with signed Content Credentials. These are provenance features, not a stated license grant.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Store source URL/provider ID, uploader, original filename, representation/version/save IDs, retrieval time and provenance separately from the license record.

[INFERENCE] Search matches, public Share visibility, camera authenticity and signed origin evidence must never automatically set rights-cleared. Capture license text, scope, attribution, derivative/redistribution restrictions and permission evidence explicitly.
limitations: [uncertain] These sources do not establish a standard machine-readable stock-footage license, attribution or redistribution-rights contract in Frame.io; no blanket absence is claimed.

The December 2025 recap describes a rollout default indexing recent 30-day uploads and Enterprise-assisted historical indexing. Whether that rollout boundary still applies to every account on 2026-10-24 is [uncertain]; do not universalize it.

Search documentation still calls NLP/semantic optimization beta and is internally inconsistent about Seen By support (listed in example metadata but unsupported in the FAQ). Do not promise exhaustive recall or rights-sensitive discovery completeness.
No footage or original file was downloaded and no rights clearance was performed.

observed_facts: Inherited historical baseline, documented October 14, 2024 and corroborated by current help: V4 centralizes assets with a panel-based workspace, metadata/Collections and multi-format review. It predates the requested change window and is not counted as a 2026 invention.

Current Project Navigation holds folders, Collections, Shares and C2C connections. Asset Viewer and Asset Details panels can be independently collapsed and resized. Grid/List layout, thumbnail size/aspect ratio, sort and field display provide visual versus dense-data views.

The Comparison Viewer supports two assets or two versions, including video, image, audio, PDF and MS Office, even across types. Linked zoom/playback and selection of the left/right header let reviewers compare and direct comments to the correct asset.

The July 2026 image/PDF comparison additions are static-only overlay/slider and Pixel Difference tools. Same dimensions are required for the image/PDF comparison features in the release note; the help article explicitly gives the same-dimension condition for overlay. Video side-by-side support must not be generalized into video pixel-difference support.
September 2026 release evidence documents full multi-page high-resolution InDesign previews and Spacebar Quicklook with arrow-key navigation through selected grid/list assets and folders.

The December 2025 recap documents the upgraded panel generally available for Premiere Pro 25.6: browse/manage Frame.io media, import folder structures into bins, share sequences and synchronize review comments as timeline markers. The July 2026 recap adds an After Effects panel for exporting renders and receiving comments in compositions.

Supported adjacent workflows include comment exports for FCP 10.4.0+, Media Composer, Premiere Pro and Resolve; the public integrations page names Workfront Fusion, Zapier and Make. February 2026 documents MASV server-to-server transfers specifically for Adobe-managed Enterprise accounts. July 2026 describes CuttingRoom cloud editing, Silverstack Lab v9.3 and Camera to Cloud partners.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] A complete FrameForge production can use one selection model to synchronize source bin, viewer, inspector, review thread and output evidence while keeping an NLE timeline/graph distinct from a review player's timebar.
[INFERENCE] Show static-image/PDF diff capabilities separately from temporal/video comparison so users do not infer unsupported motion-diff guarantees.
limitations: Frame.io's documented browser review player/timebar is not evidence of an integrated nonlinear editing timeline or compositing graph. Connected editors are separate documented products/workflows.

Integration announcements establish support scope, not tested connectivity or feature parity in every account/version. Native Resolve project synchronization was not established by the comment-export evidence and is not asserted.

observed_facts: Account Branding settings establish a default Share template with logo, colors and header. It applies only to newly created Shares; existing Shares are not retroactively updated. New Shares can be customized independently.

Shares can be duplicated. Project duplication excludes users/comments/Shares and optionally includes assets. These are copies and defaults with specific inheritance rules, not proof of live-linked production templates.
Account-wide metadata fields are shared definitions; asset metadata travels across copies/moves/duplicates. Dynamic folder Shares update with added/removed media; Collections are live filtered views.

July 2026 Share Lists reuse named recipient groups at account or workspace scope. The recap limits availability to Pro and above, says Content Admins create/manage them, Edit + Share members can use them, and recipients receive free Reviewer access.

Video-channel semantics are not intrinsic to Share templates or Share Lists. Metadata may describe social platform/release timing, but such labels do not themselves select or authorize an external publishing account.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Distinguish pinned production-template version, branding defaults, recipient lists and live asset views. Show exactly what a new production inherits and what is copied.
[INFERENCE] Bind channel target and credential reference per production/delivery action; never inherit external publication authority merely because a Share template or recipient list was reused.
limitations: [uncertain] These sources do not establish channel-specific OAuth credential isolation, live template migration or immutable template pinning within Frame.io. Treat those as FrameForge requirements rather than inferred Frame.io features.

observed_facts: Review evidence can target a video frame, time range, spatial anchor, PDF page or general asset. Comparison comments target the chosen left/right asset. Public versus Internal comments are explicit; internal threads remain invisible to external Share reviewers.

Mark As Complete marks feedback progress; reactions can express agreement. The comments help does not define these as an immutable sign-off on exact output bytes. Authors can edit/delete comments. Fields, including status, are editable, and a Share Featured field updates the asset's Project field.

Stacks open the newest version and can be reordered. Share Show all versions exposes either the complete stack or only its latest asset. Mounted Storage saves can attach to the latest version while keeping comments/metadata from being buried on old versions. Version label, stack identity and exact saved bytes are therefore distinct concepts.

Shares are external Frame.io review/media links. Public means visible to anyone with access to the link; Secure sharing is Enterprise-only and limits access to project members and explicitly added recipients. Share Visibility can disable access. Passphrase, expiration, comment/download permissions and all-versus-latest-version display are configurable.

Creating a Share requires sharing permission. Edit & Share permits upload/manage/share/comment/view/download; Edit removes share/download rights; Comment Only and View Only are narrower. Inherited higher permission cannot be lowered by assigning a lower Project permission. Restricted Projects break normal inheritance; Owners, Content Admins and scoped Workspace Admins retain documented access.

Account-level Share download override can disable downloads on existing links and control which roles may re-enable them. Share custom sorting is limited to the root level and Grid/List; Reel cannot be reordered directly.

All Shares exposes visibility, last-viewed/view counts and editable link options even after distribution. Share Activity records Opened Share Link, Viewed Asset, Commented and Download, with names/dates/actions. Public-link reviewers identify themselves by name/email for the session; this is not equivalent to an authenticated Secure Share identity.

March 2026 release evidence explicitly documents Workfront integration with Frame.io as the review surface, shared work-in-progress storage and end-to-end multi-stage approvals, available to Frame.io Enterprise and Workfront customers. It must not be silently generalized to every standalone Frame.io plan.

Comments can be exported/printed, including frame/page thumbnails and annotations in printable/PDF output. Exports respect current filters/search/sort. Replies do not participate in comments-panel filtering/sorting/search according to the panel help.

The documented actions above establish review, access-controlled sharing and delivery/download engagement in Frame.io. They are not evidence of a successful upload to a specific YouTube channel or of a publicly published external video. No external destination privacy state, OAuth grant or quota contract is verified by creating a Share.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Bind a sign-off to production ID, provider asset ID, version/save ID, exact artifact digest, approver identity, decision and time. Revoke the applicability of that sign-off after artifact-affecting edits even if a live Share URL stays unchanged.

[INFERENCE] Keep separate states for reviewed, approved, shared, delivery/download observed, uploaded, processing complete and publicly published. Require channel/destination ID, intended visibility, credential scope, upload receipt and destination read-back before claiming publication.

[INFERENCE] After changing a Share, read back visibility, selected version/save, recipients and download/security policy. Preserve an evidence snapshot; a mutable activity feed is not automatically a tamper-proof approval ledger.
limitations: [uncertain] Automatic invalidation of an Approved status/sign-off after a new stack version, reordered version or Mounted Storage save is not established in these sources. Do not claim approval is automatically byte-bound or automatically invalidated.

[uncertain] Per-version immutable approval audit retention, exact content-hash binding and legally authenticated public-link sign-off are not established. Editable status/comment semantics cannot substitute for them.

[uncertain] Native direct channel upload/publication capabilities were not established by this source set; this is an evidence boundary, not a claim that no connector can publish. Current YouTube privacyStatus/OAuth/quota specifics belong to the dedicated YouTube research and are not invented here.

The API guide and user help differ in completeness around Workspace Admin access to Restricted Projects. The richer current user-help exception is retained; account-role PATCH is explicitly experimental in the API guide. No permission mutation or authenticated read-back was executed.

observed_facts: Documentation provides Ctrl/Cmd+K search; Enter in the global search opens the first result rather than submitting a traditional form. Range comments support I/O points and Esc returns from range playback to full playback.

September 2026 Quicklook supports Spacebar on a selected asset and arrow-key traversal through Grid/List. Comment cards navigate to their timestamp and spatial pin/annotation; Internal comments have a lock icon and active anchored-comment controls change visual state.

Panels can be resized and independently collapsed. Grid/List, thumbnail size and aspect ratio adapt information density. Image/PDF viewing includes zoom and minimaps; fullscreen review retains commenting tools.

March 2026 adds Cmd+scroll/pinch zoom and two-finger panning, with cursor/gesture-centered focal points. July 2026 documents an iOS redesign with updated menus and multilingual support; February 2026 documents richer mobile search-match context. These are documented mobile features, not runtime observations.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Keep keyboard selection and the selected artifact/version visible across panels, provide non-drag alternatives for range/stack operations, and distinguish keyboard commands by context so Spacebar does not ambiguously launch Quicklook and playback.
[INFERENCE] Use resizable/collapsible panels and dense/visual modes but separately verify keyboard focus order, screen-reader names, color-independent status and narrow-screen reflow in FrameForge.
limitations: [uncertain] End-to-end keyboard reachability, focus restoration/trapping, screen-reader interoperability, contrast, WCAG compliance and exact responsive breakpoints are not established by these sources. No accessibility audit or mobile/browser runtime test was performed.
